notes:
Summary: Polaris builds a SaaS contact center layer that layers RAG over customers' existing KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, S3). They want agent-assist + automated ticket summarization + tool-calling (CRUD operations into ticketing) with deterministic citations and freshness guarantees. Strong compliance needs (EU data residency for enterprise customers).

Key requirements: retrieval latency target <200ms median for KB lookups; sustained throughput 800 req/min with headroom to handle 3x spikes; provenance links surfaced in agent UI (citation URL + excerpt + score); TTL/freshness policy: index updates within 24h for policy tickets, near-real-time for incident docs; multi-source retrieval (fused results from vector DB + enterprise search + S3 blobs) with de-dup and source ranking. Must support SSO (SAML), org KMS, audit logs and retention controls.

Model & runtime preferences: open model family allowed if reproducible; prefer ability to route to quantized local fallback model for spikes to maintain availability and cost controls. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching, KV cache sizing, per-route latency SLOs.

Quote from CTO (Adam Foster): "Deterministic citations are not optional — auditors will ask. We need a chain of provenance we can show in logs."

POC goals (success metrics): 1) citation precision >= 88% on sampled tickets, 2) median retrieval+generation latency <300ms at 1x load and <600ms at 3x spike, 3) end-to-end failure rate <0.5% over 48h stress run, 4) accurate tool-call emulation with safe-guards.

Business notes: cost-sensitive — interested in a hybrid billing model (baseline dedicated capacity + overage pricing). Prior vendors evaluated: Zendesk RAG beta, internal embeddings pipeline (high maintenance).

technical_notes:
Indexer plan: hybrid pipeline — incremental vector updates for tickets, live sync for incident docs. Retrieval fusion: candidate set from vector DB, supplement with enterprise search hits; apply source re-ranking with freshness weight, de-dup on doc id.
Fallback strategy: route to local quantized model (distilled LLM) if latency & queue depth exceed threshold; mark answers as 'approximate' in UI.
Operational requirements: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakouts for controller, canary rollout for new kernel/quantization profiles. Need Redwood Console dashboards for token cost + per-model latency.
